title: Threnodian

{{Quote|When it comes to the Threnodian, there is a lot to tell. For now, you can think of it this way: the Threnodian is the most powerful Tacet Discord. The Battle of the Threnodian that happened before was to fend it off.|Yangyang|[[First Resonance]]}} {{Terminology Infobox |title = Threnodian |type = Lore |image = Threnodian.jpg }} '''Threnodians''' are formidable creatures born from the [[The Lament|Laments]], with the power to destroy human spirit and feed off of their collapsed will. If civilizations represent mankind's collective will, they are the embodiment of the hidden fears and inner turmoil of humanity, manifesting as destructive disasters known as [[Tacet Discord]] that spread across different parts of the world[https://wutheringwaves.kurogames.com/en/main/#lore| Wuthering Waves Official Site]. ==Overview== Threnodians are a reflection of the collective fears of humanity condensed into physical form, born from the dark side of collective consciousnesses. Each Threnodian embodies a certain fear of struggle, which has a deep connection to the area that faces them, such as [[Ovathrax]], the Threnodian of War, in [[Jinzhou]], a land that has been a battleground for centuries[[Grand Warstorm]]. Threnodians are incredibly powerful creatures, and are capable of vastly strengthening the effects of [[Waveworn Phenomenon]] on their surrounding environment. Just as a [[Sentinel]] has their own appointed Resonator whom they have resonated with, so too do Threnodians[[What Yesterday Wept, Today Doth Sing]]. However, the exact process of becoming a Threnodian's Resonator, and whether all Threnodians are capable of obtaining a Resonator, is not known—as Leviathan only gained this ability after its assimilation with the Sentinel Imperator, and Aleph-1's Resonator was artificially induced. A single Threnodian's revival is never an independent occurrence, as they can sense each other through some form of telepathic link and can trigger catastrophic events across [[Solaris-3]]. After fusing with Leviathan, Sentinel Imperator gained knowledge that as long as there is human civilization, Threnodians will always exist, and Threnodians cannot be truly killed as even Leviathan itself does not know the means to do it. The only way to defeat a Threnodian is to shackle it to a Resonator. Aalto explains that due to their nature as shadows of civilization, they are both formless and immortal, thus cannot entirely be erased. Therefore, sealing it inside the Resonator's body is the next best method in defeating a Threnodian by giving them form. This was proven to be true as Leviathan was successfully sealed. For now, the threat of Threnodian is over in Rinascita and it will take some time before a new Threnodian will appear to replace the sealed Leviathan. Due to their unique nature, Cristoforo reveals that a Threnodian’s power and essence is one and the same, and he claims that if Leviathan were to possess Abby through the Dark Tide, they could merge themselves with Ovathrax and gain a complete rebirth as Abby contains the dormant powers of Ovathrax within them. [[Aemeath]] and [[Luuk Herssen]] reveal that Aleph-1 does not originate from Solaris-3 and is in fact a Threnodian from space. This suggests other Threnodians exist beyond the planet, with implications that the Lament may in fact not be a local phenomenon confined to Solaris-3, but across the universe. This is backed by the existence of [[The White Tower]], another ancient Threnodian sealed within the [[Somnoire]] that is implied to have arrived on Solaris-3 from space. ==Story== ===History=== ===Present Story=== During the [[Grand Warstorm|Jinzhou crisis]], Ovathrax's revival begins unexpectedly. After the defeat of its vanguards, [[Crownless]] and [[Dreamless]], by [[Rover]] and [[Jiyan]] with the support of the [[Midnight Rangers]] and other [[Resonators]] in Jinzhou, it opted to flee, and its current location is unknown. According to [[Black Shores]]' systems, Ovathrax's revival has triggered similar reactions in other countries, with [[Rinascita]] being the only exception, where no frequencies fluctuations related to Threnodians have been detected.[[Through the Sea Thou Break]] Aleph-1 is an extraterrestrial Threnodian that was drifting between the space of the [[Homeland Civilization]] and [[Solaris-3]], before intercepting the [[Exostrider]] Baldur. The two behemoths engaged in battle, with Baldur (after resonating with [[Aemeath]]) sealing Aleph-1 above Solaris-3 past the [[Stridergate]], a rare opening in the Etheric Sea that allows access to outer space. Baldur landed in the Roya Frostlands, providing warmth and guidance to the Royan people before becoming dormant. During Rover's arrival in Lahai-Roi, Aleph-1 attempted to break past the Stridergate and devour Solaris. After Aemeath sacrificed herself to travel back in time through [[Voidspace]] in order to pilot the [[Exostrider]] and seal it underneath [[Sundermere]] as part of a closed loop, it was pursued and defeated by Rover and the combined efforts of [[Startorch Academy]], the [[Spacetrek Collective]], and the newly-awakened [[Exostrider]]. After being defeated by the Exostrider, it was cast out to the edge of the known universe, majorly stalling its return. (True form remains sealed within the Somnoire) |Unknown |} [[Ashinohara]] has a Threnodian whose power comes and goes in predictable cycles. It caused Honami City to vanish with a then-new power, and thus is implicated in the recent disappearance of Ashinohara as a whole. [[Chongzhou]] is known to have a ThrenodianQiuyuan Resonance Evaluation Report: "It has now been confirmed that the individual in question has no connection to the Sentinel or Threnodian of Chongzhou.". [[The White Tower]] remains a particularly unique case among Threnodians, implied to be another alien Threnodian similar to [[Aleph-1]]. It was preserved in the [[Somnoire]] by the ancient civilization that it destroyed, as it slipped inside and eventually caused the fracturing of the Somnoire into its present day layers. As this Threnodian attempted to reconstruct both itself and the shattered memories of the civilisation, it has possibly gained a "soul" in the form of [[D]], master of the cinema layer - though this remains ambiguous, and the original Threnodian may still be sealed inside. ==Trivia== ===Etymology=== *'Threnodian' is an adjective that refers to something that is mournful or related to a threnody, which is a song, poem, or speech expressing sorrow, especially for someone who has died. It often describes artistic expression that embodies themes of grief or lamentation. ==Other Languages== {{Other Languages |en = Threnodian |zhs = 鸣式 |zht = 鳴式 |ja = 鳴式 |ko = 명식 |es = Trenodiano |fr = Le Réprimantum |de = Threnodiane |th = เธรโนเดียน |pt = Trenodiano }} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Navigation== {{Lore Navbox|Terminology}} [[Category:Terminology]] [[Category:Lore]] [[zh:鸣式]] [[ru:Плакальщик]]
